title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler models a column of height h with y(0)=y(h)=0. An auxiliary horizontal force C produces an initial deflection angle α = y'(0). The constant g = GO is the horizontal offset of the centre of gravity, fixed by the side condition gh = ∫_0^h y dx.

End of §24: imposing y(h)=0 and gh = ∫_0^h y dx and eliminating g gives one relation between C, α and the fixed data. That relation determines α as a function of C.

§25: Euler observes that this relation can admit α ≠ 0 even when C = 0. Those parameter values are the critical case: the height at which the column begins to bend, and then breaks, under its own weight alone. In modern terms this is the eigenvalue / bifurcation formulation of self-weight buckling. Buckling is detected as a nontrivial solution of the homogeneous boundary-value problem.

§26 (C = 0): the integro-differential equation is
  g x + ∫_0^x x dy + m y'' = 0,  with m = e b² (flexural rigidity, EI).
Differentiating gives m y''' + x y' + g = 0. With u = y' this is m u'' + x u = −g, an inhomogeneous Airy-type equation.

Euler tries the power series y = Σ a_n x^n with a_1 = α:
- At x = 0 the equation gives m y''(0) = 0, so β = a_2 = 0.
- The recurrence is m(n+3)(n+2)(n+1) a_{n+3} = −n a_n, with a_3 = −g/(6m).
- Exponents step by 3, so the coefficients split into three residue classes mod 3:
  - 3n+2: all vanish (seeded by β = 0);
  - 3n+1: multiples of α;
  - 3n: multiples of g.

This is exactly Euler's claim. It prepares §27, where y = αp + gq with p = x − x⁴/(2·3·4·m) + … and q = −x³/(6m) + …. Then y(h)=0 and gh = ∫y give a 2×2 homogeneous linear system in (α, g). Its vanishing determinant is the critical-height condition.

The series p and q are entire functions of Airy/Bessel type. In closed form they are combinations of x^{1/2}J_{±1/3}(c x^{3/2}) and integrals thereof, the functions Greenhill used in 1881.
errors: No algebraic error on this page: β=0 and the mod-3 splitting of the coefficients follow correctly from Euler's equation.

Possible modelling issue (not checkable from this page alone): the standard self-weight moment, with x from the base and unit weight per length, is ∫_x^h (y(s)−y(x)) ds. Euler's moment term gx + xy − ∫_0^x y dx differs from it. It depends on his particular end conditions and reaction conventions set up on earlier pages. The later literature (Truesdell's account, Greenhill 1881) regards Euler's 1778 treatment of self-weight buckling as not yielding the correct critical height. This page's derivation inherits whatever is in the setup.
Minor: 'differentio-differentialis' is apt, but the equation also contains the integral ∫x dy. It is really integro-differential, equivalent to a third-order ODE plus the condition y''(0)=0.

ideas.what: Critical load/height characterized as the parameter value at which a nonzero deflection exists with zero lateral force (homogeneous problem has nontrivial solution)

ideas.what: Buckling of a column under its own weight; maximal height a column can sustain

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up the well-known (and historically discussed) Euler 1778 self-weight column problem. The Airy-type series and the mod-3 coefficient structure are routine and are already recognized by historians (Truesdell) as Bessel-type series in Euler's column work. Nothing new beyond the documented record.
